stock_pulse.description: Set stock inching pulse and width in milliseconds; automatic relay action follows.

stock_startup.advanced_reason: Changes what the mains load does after a later power cut; on/stay can energize it without anyone present.
stock_startup.description: Set stock power-recovery behavior on/off/stay, not an immediate relay toggle.

stock_switch_off.advanced_reason: Attended mains relay write: removing power can interrupt the attached appliance; confirm identity and read back state.
stock_switch_off.body_transform: stock_envelope and stock_crypto; never use the DIY object envelope.

stock_switch_on.description: Stock single-channel switch=on; attended mains write.

stock_switches_set.advanced_reason: Changes a selected mains channel. Require attended selection and confirm outlet/state to avoid actuating a different load.

stock_switches_set.description: Set one outlet in a stock multi-channel switches array.

txt_match.description: Required by the stock app; use type=diy_plug plus apivers=1 to select official DIY.

methods.notes: Accept eWeLink_ and eWelink_ case variants and take deviceid after the first eight instance characters. Use resolved IPv4 and SRV port; append 8081 only if no SRV port is available. Concatenate present data1..data4 in order before Base64/JSON decoding. TXT id can name a bridge child and differ from the instance deviceid.

mdns_txt_match.description: The app requires a TXT type; type=diy_plug selects the documented DIY variant rather than stock.

identification.notes: Instance eWeLink_<deviceid> or eWelink_<deviceid>; SRV port is authoritative. 8081 is only a missing-port fallback, never an override.

device.name: Sonoff / eWeLink LAN Relays
device.notes:
SCOPE: stock eWeLink LAN relays using /zeroconf/switch, switches, startup, pulse and getState, plus the explicitly documented Basic R3/RFR3/Mini DIY variant. Other UIIDs, lights, fans, RF bridges and metering are not asserted.
STOCK IS NOT DIY. Stock requests carry sequence, deviceid, selfApikey, iv, encrypt and a STRING data field; encrypted stock uses raw-MD5(devicekey) AES-128-CBC. Official DIY uses only deviceid and an OBJECT data field with no stock encryption metadata. A plaintext stock response must never be treated as proof of DIY support, and the stock envelope must not be sent to DIY mode.
Integration is identify_only because stock needs a dedicated TXT/SRV, devicekey, Base64-IV, AES envelope and per-UIID dispatcher. The DIY commands are separated explicitly; generic consumers must not route every _ewelink service to them by default.

openness.notes: DIY is officially documented. Stock encrypted LAN is not the DIY protocol and is recovered from the vendor app and public clients.

upstream_docs.covers: Only the documented Basic R3/RFR3/Mini DIY discovery, plaintext objects and local endpoints; stock encryption is separately recovered.

exclusivity.recovery: The small HTTP server is effectively single-threaded; serialize requests and briefly retry ECONNRESET rather than opening concurrent posts.

pairing.notes: Stock and DIY have different authorization answers. Do not downgrade stock encrypt=true to plaintext, and do not require a devicekey from documented DIY.

pin.notes: Stock needs deviceid/devicekey normally supplied by the eWeLink account or bounded setup AP. Documented DIY has no pairing credential.

unpair.clears: No per-client stock bond or DIY bond is created. Account unbinding/reset is not a per-client revoke.

Account selfApikey for stock envelopes; no credential is issued in DIY
credentials.notes: AP /ap and DIY /zeroconf/wifi use HTTP JSON without transport encryption. Stock AES-CBC has no MAC and its IV is Base64 transport, not a password. Protect the setup AP/LAN and never log devicekey, selfApikey or Wi-Fi secrets.
stored_on_device: Wi-Fi credentials and regional dispatch settings
Stock devicekey/account binding or DIY mode state

methods.description: Only Basic R3, RFR3 and Mini on DIY-capable firmware (3.3.0+; 3.5.0 uses the device AP web page). Enable DIY by the model/document-specific procedure and use keyless deviceid/data-object requests.

steps.action: Confirm the exact model/firmware is in ITEAD's published DIY scope and enable DIY using that document's AP/jumper procedure.
steps.expect: TXT advertises type=diy_plug and apivers=1; no stock encrypt flag is required.

steps.action: Use the resolved SRV port and POST only {deviceid, data:{...}}; no sequence, selfApikey, iv or encrypt field is added.

setup.notes: Stock setup uses eWeLink account binding. Its devicekey normally comes from the account device list; on bounded stock setup-AP flows that expose it, GET 10.10.7.1/device can supply deviceid/apikey before normal app setup. That is not universal recovery or a promise for an already configured unit. Official DIY applies only to Basic R3/RFR3/Mini on supported firmware.

rejoin.notes: The top-level default records that an in-place route exists where the exact model/mode supports one; it is not a universal stock no-reset promise. The consumer selects the model-specific path below. BASICR2/RFR2 stock still requires its already model-scoped reset procedure above. Verified DIY is the explicit in-place exception; other stock models use their own setup flow rather than inheriting either a universal reset or no-reset rule.

steps.action: Select the rejoin path from the exact advertised model and stock-versus-DIY mode instead of applying the top-level default to every stock unit.
steps.expect: The BASICR2/RFR2 reset path, another stock model's documented setup path, or the verified DIY in-place path is selected deliberately.

steps.action: For BASICR2/RFR2 stock, use factory_reset.procedures[0], the model-scoped five-second reset, before provisioning the new network; do not apply that hold to other models.
steps.expect: BASICR2/RFR2 enters quick pairing as its own manual requires.

steps.action: For verified DIY only, POST /zeroconf/wifi with the new SSID/password without a factory reset, then rediscover.
steps.expect: The DIY device joins the new network; instance deviceid and SRV port are rechecked.

steps.action: Retry the cached stock devicekey but do not assume it survived re-pairing; retrieve it through the legitimate account/bounded setup source if changed.

testing.notes: No relay, mDNS browse, setup AP, encrypted request or DIY operation was run by this project. Facts are reported from eWeLink 5.27.0 static analysis, ITEAD DIY protocol v1.4/v2.0 and SonoffLAN 73690b7. Vectors use an invented devicekey and IV; no stock account or physical relay was used.

evidence.documentation_review: ITEAD DIY v1.4/v2.0 supplies the Basic R3/RFR3/Mini-only keyless object API, 249-byte TXT splitting, 200 ms request spacing and OTA. local_access.summary: Stock devices with a legitimate cached devicekey work over mDNS/HTTP locally; the three documented DIY models work keylessly with the simpler object API.

commands.getState: Read with empty params at /zeroconf/getState; not universal and may answer text/html.
commands.pulse: Inching: {pulse:'on'|'off',pulseWidth:n} at /zeroconf/pulse. DIY documents 500..36000000 ms in multiples of 500; stock per-UIID limits may differ.
response_quirks: SPM-Main can send empty data; ZBBridge-U can omit data.
RF Bridge can contain a malformed '=' where ':' belongs; repair only that exact reported prefix pattern.

Some plaintext retains trailing 0x02 bytes from a firmware padding bug. CBC decryption is unauthenticated; after normal PKCS#7 validation/removal, strip only those exact trailing 0x02 bytes. Never strip arbitrary JSON bytes or call a successful decode authenticated.
commands.startup: Power recovery behavior: {startup:'on'|'off'|'stay'} at /zeroconf/startup; multi-channel uses configure/startups arrays.

diy_mode.discovery: _ewelink._tcp with type=diy_plug and apivers=1; use SRV port (8081 is only its common default).
diy_mode.envelope: {"deviceid":"<deviceid>","data":{...}} where data is an object. No sequence, selfApikey, iv or encrypt field and no AES.
diy_mode.local_ota: ota_unlock then ota_flash {downloadUrl,sha256sum}; HTTP server must support Range. Older DIY documentation can require a vendor unlock service. Both commands are advanced.
diy_mode.scope: Official Basic R3, RFR3 and Mini on DIY firmware 3.3.0+; firmware 3.5.0 enables from AP web page. No other stock model is implied.

mdns.diy_state: type=diy_plug apivers=1 with plaintext JSON data and no devicekey.
mdns.instance_regex: ^eWelink_[0-9a-fA-F]{10}$ (case-insensitive eWeLink/eWelink prefix; preserve the deviceid suffix case as published).
mdns.port_rule: Use SRV port and resolved IPv4. Use 8081 only when SRV supplies no usable port; never replace a present non-8081 SRV port.
mdns.stock_state: If encrypt is true/'true', Base64-decode iv and the joined ciphertext then AES-decrypt. Otherwise parse the joined JSON directly. Missing/empty data is not a JSON document; some models omit it.
mdns.txt_rule: Concatenate data1, data2, data3, data4 in numeric order while present. Each chunk is at most 249 bytes. seq orders state updates and can reset on reboot.

setup_ap.credential_boundary: Use the bounded AP read only while the device is in setup mode and only when the response actually exposes both fields. It is not universal recovery for configured devices.
setup_ap.get_device: GET /device returns metadata and, only on bounded stock flows that expose them, deviceid and apikey/devicekey.
setup_ap.post_ap: POST /ap JSON {ssid,password,serverName,port}. serverName/port select the intended dispatch service; this is not a local-only cloud bypass.

stock_crypto.algorithm: AES-128-CBC with PKCS#7. key = raw 16-byte MD5(UTF-8 devicekey), not MD5 hex ASCII and not the UUID text directly.
stock_crypto.ciphertext: Standard Base64 of AES(JSON.stringify(params) UTF-8 with PKCS#7). No MAC or replay authentication is provided: successful CBC decryption, valid padding or a valid JSON parse proves decodability only, never sender authenticity or message integrity.
stock_crypto.iv: 16 raw bytes on the wire as Base64. The app generates 16 decimal digits; public clients use arbitrary random 16 bytes. Base64-decode inbound iv before CBC.

fields.data: STRING. Encrypted mode: Base64 AES ciphertext. Plaintext stock mode: JSON.stringify(params), not a nested object.
fields.deviceid: Ten-hex-character device id from the instance/account, not necessarily TXT id for a child.
fields.encrypt: Boolean copied from TXT encrypt true/'true'; never force false on encrypted stock.
fields.iv: Base64 of 16 raw IV bytes, sent in encrypted and plaintext stock modes.
fields.selfApikey: Logged-in account API key; device-side validation is unverified, so it is not a substitute for devicekey.
fields.sequence: String epoch milliseconds truncated to 13 characters; unique/monotonic per sender.

stock_envelope.response: Require error=0 and sequence/seq correlation where supplied. Encrypted response data is Base64 AES with its own Base64 iv; plaintext quirks are listed below.
stock_envelope.serialization: One request at a time; the reviewed app timeout is 15 s. SonoffLAN briefly retries ECONNRESET. getState is not universal: text/html means the device is online but supplied no JSON state.
stock_envelope.url: POST http://<ipv4>:<srv-port>/zeroconf/<cmd>; Accept application/json, Content-Type application/json;charset=UTF-8, Connection close, minimal headers.

remaining_unknowns: Stock encrypted response envelope details across models, literal TXT encrypt/iv rotation and sequence/selfApikey validation.
Whether stock devicekey changes on reset/re-pairing and which exact setup-AP models expose apikey at /device.
Per-UIID support and pulse-width limits, multi-channel startup/configure arrays and universal getState behavior.
Long-term stock LAN behavior with WAN blocked and model/firmware availability of DIY mode beyond the three documented products.
Factory-reset procedures and state survival outside BASICR2/RFR2; no cross-family hold is invented.
